Pros: Interviewing with Bolt consisted of 45 conversations with leaders and stakeholders I'd be working alongside on a daily basis/supporting. Interviewers were engaging and it was a very positive experience overall. Once hired, onboarding took about 12 weeks and was very organized. Had more than enough support in terms of both materials and colleagues to get up to speed on Bolt's product, culture, etc. Pay and benefits are strong  company is remotefirst, Pay is competitive at/above industry average, and benefits are in alignment with other tech companies in the space. Despite previous restructures and changes in the organization the last few years, leaders are/have been transparent about the changes, the reasons behind them, and the vision/plan for Bolt moving forward. Product is interesting and a disrupter in the ecommerce space. You'll have the opportunity to work on/support the development of a product that supports well known brands everyone knows which is cool. There have been changes in leadership recently, and as a new hire, it seems from both a company vision/GTM strategy, as well as an employee morale standpoint, they are for the better. Individual contributors and leaders alike are aligned on the vision for the company and the product moving forward and are making a concerted effort to create a culture of more communication, transparency, and openness within all aspects of the organization. Definitely a startup culture where they prioritize hiring individuals who are able to/enjoy working autonomously, are strong culture builders, optimistic, and take ownership and accountability on the work they contribute. While there are more than enough systems/processes put in place, you also will have the opportunity to create processes from scratch or iterate on them. This may not be for everyone, but if you enjoy working in a high growth/scrappy startup environment, you will likely enjoy the type of work you get to do here.
Cons: Because of the multiple changes that have been made in the last 612 months, there may be some people that may not be aligned with the new vision/strategy of the company or new leadership moving forward. That being said, leadership has made a concerted effort to address this misalignment head on and have candid conversations about the future rather than not addressing people's apprehensions. From everything I've seen, department leaders and the executive team have taken a very humanistic approach to addressing people's concerns, and you can/will be heard and seen as a valued member of the Bolt organization.

Pros: Smart, collaborative people and an excellent executive leadership team Great market opportunity and strong company growth potential Anybody at the company can have outsize impact Cultural norms and tooling allow for teams and individuals to easily provide feedback positive & constructive to one another, and feedback is nearly always given appropriate consideration regardless of who is giving the feedback to whom.  Solid pay & benefits compared to companies of similar size and funding
Cons: Like many highgrowth startups, the environment is fastpaced, change is regular, everybody has a lot on their plate, and some parts of the organization are more mature in their processes and decisionmaking than others.  To that end, being successful at Bolt requires you to: Be highly thoughtful about what is a priority and what can be accomplished over a specific time frame, and be comfortable saying "no" to projects or goals that are unrealistic or not yet a priority.  Take time to build foundations, organizing information & data so that team members can make decisions quickly and then disseminate information about those decisions to key stakeholders with high efficiency.Currently, not every team or every individual makes the time to do the above on a regular basis, which can result in friction between teams and individuals. However, over the course of my time at the company, people have improved in these regards significantly and I have little doubt that we will only get better as time goes on.
